finding.claim: When a token has no iat, the verifier cache stores no exp-based expiry, so an expired token is still accepted from cache for up to cacheTTL (default 600000 ms) after its exp passes.
finding.source: Token string with exp but no iat (issuer used noTimestamp: true), passed to verify with cache enabled.
finding.sink: Cache-hit path in verify() returns the cached payload without re-checking exp.

trace.note: cacheSet: hasIat is false, so the exp branch at lines 123-129 is skipped.
cacheValue[2] is 0, so it becomes maxTTL = clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + cacheTTL.
Cache lookup for the token hash.
Cache-hit condition checks only now <= max, not exp.
Default cacheTTL is 600000 ms.

finding.guards_checked: Cache is opt-in (createCache returns null unless cache is set, verifier.js:83-86, 580). The exp validator (verifier.js:606-614) runs only on the first, uncached verification. The max-TTL cap is applied, but exp is never folded into it when iat is missing.

finding.claim: Claim validators for aud, iss, sub, jti, nonce, and maxAge (iat) are silently skipped when the claim is absent, so a validly signed token without aud passes an allowedAud check unless requiredClaims is set.
finding.source: Validly signed token whose payload lacks aud (or iss, sub, jti, nonce, iat).
finding.sink: verifyToken validator loop (verifier.js:304-323), which enforces allowedAud, allowedIss, allowedSub, allowedJti, allowedNonce, and maxAge.

trace.note: requiredClaims is enforced only when the operator passes it.
if (!(claim in payload)) continue skips the validator for any absent claim.
allowedJti, allowedAud, allowedIss, allowedSub, allowedNonce validators are registered here.
maxAge validator on iat is registered here.

finding.guards_checked: Signature is verified first (verifier.js:280), so the attacker must hold a token signed with the same key. The comment at lines 309-310 assumes requiredClaims covers absence, which is only true if the operator set it (verifier.js:496, 561-563).

finding.claim: The signature segment accepts any base64url character in the final position, so non-canonical encodings (differing only in unused trailing bits) verify as distinct token strings for the same signature.
finding.source: Attacker alters the last base64url character of a valid token's signature segment.
finding.sink: verifySignature decodes the signature with Buffer.from(..., 'base64') (crypto.js:339), which ignores unused trailing bits.

trace.note: BASE64URL_RE is /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/ and does not check canonical trailing bits.
Signature segment is checked only against that regex.
Signature is the substring after the last dot.
Signature is decoded with Buffer.from(signature,'base64'), which drops unused bits.

finding.guards_checked: Base64url alphabet check (decoder.js:35-43) and HMAC timingSafeEqual (crypto.js:343). The signature itself is not forged. Impact requires the application to key on the raw token string, for example a denylist or replay cache.

finding.claim: With cache enabled, verify() throws a TypeError for Buffer tokens because hashToken calls token.split, which Buffer does not have; the exception escapes even in callback or promise mode.
finding.source: Token passed as a Buffer (accepted by the type check at verifier.js:353).
finding.sink: cacheKeyBuilder(token) (default hashToken) is called before decoding.

trace.note: Buffer tokens pass the type check.
cache.get(cacheKeyBuilder(token)) runs before decode.
hashToken calls token.split('.', 1), which is not a Buffer method.

finding.guards_checked: Cache enabled is required (verifier.js:580). No try/catch around the cache lookup. Impact is availability and error-type only.

finding.claim: A cached TokenError never records a min time, so a cached FAST_JWT_INACTIVE error is returned until errorCacheTTL expires even after nbf has passed.
finding.source: Token with a future nbf, verified once while inactive, with a large errorCacheTTL.
finding.sink: Cache-hit path returns the cached error (verifier.js:368-377).

trace.note: TokenError branch sets only cacheValue[2]; cacheValue[1] stays 0.
min === 0 makes the cache-hit condition true regardless of now.
max = clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + errorCacheTTL.

finding.guards_checked: With the default errorCacheTTL (-1) the cached entry expires almost immediately, so impact requires an operator-set large errorCacheTTL. Availability only.

finding.claim: In async key mode with complete: true, the result's input is the full token including the signature, while the sync path returns the signing input (header.payload). This is inconsistent and breaks callers that re-verify input.
finding.source: Token verified with a key function and complete: true.
finding.sink: Return value of the async verify callback.

trace.note: Async path returns input: token (full token).
Sync path returns decoded input, which decoder.js:70 sets to header.payload only.
input = token.slice(0, lastSeparator), the signing input.

finding.guards_checked: Not a security boundary by itself. Correctness and consistency only.
